take_homes: Licences issued and licences actually used are two different numbers, and I have only ever been shown the first one.
Before any rollout, ask what the person does today instead, and what would have to be true for them to drop it.
An agent doesn't carry its accountability with it. If no one is named as owner, that gap is the finding.

monday.move: Ask my controller how she writes the month-end variance commentary today and what would make her drop that way. Ask IT how many of the current licences were actually used last month.
monday.when: Tuesday, 15 minutes after the close meeting
monday.stop_condition: If her current process takes under an hour and she is content with it, I drop the idea. If IT can't show usage numbers, I stop and ask why not.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: Access is cheap and reported as success, while use depends on trust and time. That is more than buying a licence. Nothing in the day put a cost or payback on building that capability, so I'm not convinced yet.

one_line: Good on why a licence isn't the same as people using it, but there was no cost or payback figure all day and too much talking before I did anything.
